topic: 6.3 billion dollars in crypto lost in 20 minute hack
headline_marked: 6.3 billion dollars [[stolen from Binance in 20 minutes]]
headline: 6.3 billion dollars stolen from Binance in 20 minutes
summary: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange suffered one of the biggest digital currency thefts in history, with hackers targeting its transaction wallets.
details: Hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world's largest exchange, in just 20 minutes. This is being described as one of the largest digital currency thefts in history.

According to Binance, the attack began after Thursday, October 29, at 8 PM local time. The hackers managed to gain control of the exchange's 'signing infrastructure,' allowing them to authorize unauthorized transfers from several wallets.

Binance initially suspected a compromised laptop, but further investigations revealed multiple security vulnerabilities. The company stated that they have a $1 billion Bitcoin reserve fund to compensate users for losses.

TRM Labs, a US-based blockchain analysis firm, noted that the attack shares characteristics with previous cyber operations linked to North Korean hackers. However, Binance co-CEO Richard Teng has stated that the identity of the attackers has not yet been confirmed.

About half of the stolen assets, primarily stablecoins like USDT and USDC, have already been frozen by issuers. However, approximately $2.4 billion in Bitcoin and Ether remains missing and beyond the reach of central authorities.

Because Bitcoin and Ether are decentralized, they cannot be frozen by a single entity. Recovery depends on whether the hackers move these assets to an exchange or broker that is willing to cooperate with law enforcement.
The company's co-CEO Richard Teng confirmed that losses will be covered by the company's own assets and its specialized security fund to ensure user funds are protected.
caption:
6.3 billion dollars gone in just 20 minutes. One of the biggest crypto heists in history has hit Binance.

Hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world's largest exchange, in just 20 minutes. This is being described as one of the largest digital currency thefts in history.

According to Binance, the attack began after Thursday, October 29, at 8 PM local time. The hackers managed to gain control of the exchange's 'signing infrastructure,' allowing them to authorize unauthorized transfers from several wallets.

Binance initially suspected a compromised laptop, but further investigations revealed multiple security vulnerabilities. The company stated that they have a $1 billion Bitcoin reserve fund to compensate users for losses.

TRM Labs, a US-based blockchain analysis firm, noted that the attack shares characteristics with previous cyber operations linked to North Korean hackers. However, Binance co-CEO Richard Teng has stated that the identity of the attackers has not yet been confirmed.

About half of the stolen assets, primarily stablecoins like USDT and USDC, have already been frozen by issuers. However, approximately $2.4 billion in Bitcoin and Ether remains missing and beyond the reach of central authorities.

Because Bitcoin and Ether are decentralized, they cannot be frozen by a single entity. Recovery depends on whether the hackers move these assets to an exchange or broker that is willing to cooperate with law enforcement.

The company's co-CEO Richard Teng confirmed that losses will be covered by the company's own assets and its specialized security fund to ensure user funds are protected.

headline_marked: Former Air Force officer [[Tahsif Souri jumped into Turag River]] while fleeing men in uniform
headline: Former Air Force officer Tahsif Souri jumped into Turag River while fleeing men in uniform
summary: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) is probing the death of KM Tahsif Souri after his friend claimed they were chased by uniformed men before the jump.
details: Former Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri died after jumping into the Turag River on October 27. His body was recovered from the Rajabari ferry terminal area on October 28.
Tahsif's friend, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip, who was taken into custody for questioning, told investigators that they were chased by several people wearing uniforms near the riverbank.
According to Dip, while they were talking at Mazar Basti, the uniformed men began chasing them, leading Tahsif to jump into the river while Dip managed to escape.
PBI investigators visited the spot near boundary pillar 29 of the Turag River in Tongi, where Dip recounted the events of the night.
A motorcycle, believed to belong to Tahsif, was recovered from the area by the PBI after it had remained parked on the road for two days.
The PBI stated they are not yet fully convinced by Dip's account and are continuing the investigation, considering all aspects of the case.
Tahsif's father, Enayetul Karim, has demanded a fair investigation into his son's death, calling the police chase account 'ridiculous'.
caption:
A former Air Force officer jumped into a river to escape men in uniform—now his friend's testimony is under scrutiny.

Former Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri died after jumping into the Turag River on October 27. His body was recovered from the Rajabari ferry terminal area on October 28.

Tahsif's friend, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip, who was taken into custody for questioning, told investigators that they were chased by several people wearing uniforms near the riverbank.

According to Dip, while they were talking at Mazar Basti, the uniformed men began chasing them, leading Tahsif to jump into the river while Dip managed to escape.

PBI investigators visited the spot near boundary pillar 29 of the Turag River in Tongi, where Dip recounted the events of the night.

A motorcycle, believed to belong to Tahsif, was recovered from the area by the PBI after it had remained parked on the road for two days.

The PBI stated they are not yet fully convinced by Dip's account and are continuing the investigation, considering all aspects of the case.

Tahsif's father, Enayetul Karim, has demanded a fair investigation into his son's death, calling the police chase account 'ridiculous'.
